title: Vendor-neutral DDIL test and conformance harness for tactical software (link emulation, multi-node TAK/CoT sync scoring, pre-Jailbreak API contract tests, TAK plugin RBAC/audit conformance)
version_designed_for: NARROWER VERSION ONLY. G29 was KILLED as a venture (G29-score.json verdict 'kill', confidence HIGH: no requirement owner, program office, budget line or vehicle; the government resources DDIL test and conformance itself through C5ISR Center Radio Rodeo / NetModX, ATEC and the APG/Huntsville software integration labs, and - new this session - the Reveille Forge Integrated Development Environment opened in July 2026 (Breaking Defense 2026-07, FACT/MEDIUM)). This diligence therefore designs the residual form named in the score file: an OPEN-SOURCE 'TAK DDIL bench' (containerised ATAK-CIV / TAK Server nodes behind Linux tc/netem or EMANE/CORE link profiles from 1 Mbps to 1 kbps with scripted partitions and reconnect storms, a sync scorer, a CoT/TAK Mission API and public-Lattice-schema contract-test CLI) plus an ATAK plugin RBAC/audit/SBOM conformance module that emits a signed OSCAL-style bundle. It is sized at $30-60k and 3-4 months, is explicitly a credibility and validation asset and a small fixed-fee readiness service, NOT a venture-scale company, and every plan and milestone below is built to TEST the decisive doubt: does a named sponsor with a budget line or vehicle exist (PdM Application Store and Pipeline under PM C2 Applications, DEVCOM C5ISR Center, ATEC, Reveille Forge, a Team Anduril / Team Lockheed T&E cell, TAK Product Center, or paying Jailbreak-series vendors) within 90 days of first demo? If the kill criteria trip, the founders stop at the open-source release, keep the relationships and put the remaining capital elsewhere. Nothing here is a legal determination on ITAR/EAR/FOCI/SBIR/immigration; constraints are described for counsel.

architecture.prose: INPUTS. Three input classes enter the bench: (1) a scenario file (YAML) that declares a link profile - bandwidth from 1 Mbps down to 1 kbps as in the DARPA FLUID regime (darpa.mil 2025-03-28, FACT/HIGH), latency, jitter, loss, and a timed schedule of partitions and reconnect storms across a named node topology; (2) synthetic traffic - a CoT generator that emits position, chat, markers, mission-data-sync objects and simulated sensor tracks (MAVLink-derived UAS positions from ArduPilot SITL converted to CoT), with a ground-truth ledger of every object, its priority tag and emission time; (3) the system under test (SUT) - a vendor's ATAK plugin APK, a CoT feed/gateway, a TAK Server Mission API client, or a Lattice SDK client exercised against the free Lattice Sandbox (developer.anduril.com sandboxes page, FACT/HIGH that sandboxes exist; licence terms not retrievable this session - EGRESS_BLOCKED). Public schemas (CoT XML event schema, TAK Protocol Version 1 protobuf, TAK Server Marti REST / Mission API documentation, Lattice protobufs on the Buf Schema Registry) and role/tag fixtures (synthetic users, roles and data tags) are the fourth input. COMPUTE. The whole bench runs on one commodity x86 host (mini PC or workstation, 32-64 GB RAM) running Docker/Podman: TAK Server containers, ATAK-CIV in Android emulators (x86_64 system images) or on a handful of physical Android phones via ADB, a netem/tc controller (or, for MANET-style topologies, an EMANE + CORE node), a capture/ledger service, the scorer and the report builder. Cloud is optional (a single large VM) for parallel runs. CORE SOFTWARE. Six modules: (a) Scenario Runner - translates the YAML into per-link tc/netem qdiscs (or EMANE event-service commands) on the container network namespaces and executes the partition schedule with wall-clock precision; (b) Traffic Generator and Ledger - emits CoT with unique IDs, priority tags and timestamps into the source nodes and records ground truth; (c) Multi-node Sync Scorer - captures what each ATAK-CIV/TAK Server node actually received (via TAK Server logs, Marti API queries and an instrumented observer plugin on the emulators) and computes time-to-arrival of priority objects, duplicates and conflicting versions after reconnect, missing objects, ordering violations and offered load versus link capacity during the reconnect storm; (d) Contract-Test Engine - drives OpenAPI-based property tests (Schemathesis-style) against a vendor's Mission API usage and buf/protobuf breaking-change and lint checks against Lattice protos, from a capture or spec; (e) Plugin Conformance Module - installs the plugin on emulator nodes, drives it with Appium/ADB scripts under synthetic roles and tagged data, and produces an RBAC matrix (which role could see/do what), an audit-event coverage table (which security-relevant actions produced a log entry, mapped to a NIST SP 800-53 AU-2-style list), a static-permission/manifest review and an SBOM (CycloneDX via Syft); (f) Report/Bundle Signer - renders HTML/JSON and an OSCAL assessment-results-style JSON bundle, signs it with Sigstore cosign. INTERFACES. CoT over TLS (TAK Server streaming port) and TAK Protocol v1 protobuf; TAK Server Marti REST / Mission API; Lattice gRPC/REST against the sandbox; Linux tc/netem via netlink and the EMANE event API; ADB/Appium to Android nodes; OSCAL, CycloneDX/SPDX and JSON out. OUTPUTS. A scored, reproducible report per run; a signed OSCAL-style conformance bundle; an SBOM; and an anonymised comparative leaderboard across SUTs. USERS. Vendor integration engineers preparing for a Jailbreak-series sprint or PdM ASaP onboarding; prime and government T&E engineers who need comparable pre-event numbers; and AO/ISSM reviewers who consume the RBAC/audit bundle. Everything is unclassified by construction; realism plateaus at 'generic DDIL' unless a lab supplies controlled waveform models or traces, which would require U.S.-person handling (constraint for counsel).

TAK Server public source (TAK-Product-Center/Server) including the takcl test framework and Mission API; LICENSE.md includes a linking provision for gRPC/protobuf libraries (github.com search summary, FACT/MEDIUM); the exact copyleft terms must be read before combining code (RECALL: GPL-family with linking exception - not re-verified this session, MEDIUM).
TAK Protocol Version 1 protobuf and CoT XML as implemented by pytak/takproto (Apache-2.0, RECALL) for the traffic generator.

Linux kernel tc/netem (in every distro) and container network namespaces for link emulation; EMANE (adjacentlink/emane, NRL-sponsored, FACT/HIGH) and CORE (coreemu/core, BSD-2-Clause, FACT/HIGH) for MANET-style topologies; Adjacent Link SRW/WNW waveform ports are NOT assumed available (controlled).

Lattice SDK protobufs published on the Buf Schema Registry (buf.build/anduril/lattice-sdk, FACT/HIGH); the language SDK repos were archived 2025-07-24 in favour of BSR-generated code (FACT/MEDIUM); the Lattice SDK License Agreement was updated 2026-07-31 (FACT/MEDIUM) but its terms were not retrievable (EGRESS_BLOCKED) - whether it permits publishing benchmark results or building third-party test tooling is UNVERIFIED and must be read before the Lattice module is released.
Lattice Sandboxes (free, simulated data) as the only runtime for the Lattice contract tests; access is at Anduril's discretion (FACT/HIGH that sandboxes exist).
Android emulator x86_64 system images (Android SDK terms) and ADB/Appium (Apache-2.0, RECALL) for driving ATAK-CIV and plugins.

Ditto SDK adapter (later stage) requires a commercial licence; small-peer developer pricing not found this session (Public evidence insufficient); AWS Marketplace lists a Cloud Sync Pro plan at $11,988 per 12 months for 1,000 connections (FACT/MEDIUM, not the SDK tier needed).
Sigstore cosign, Syft/CycloneDX for SBOM, NIST OSCAL schemas (public domain), Schemathesis/Pact-style contract tools (MIT, RECALL) for the conformance and contract modules.

A synthetic-only data regime: no PoR radio traces, SRW/WNW models or CUI ICDs; if a sponsor supplies them later, U.S.-person handling and a technology control plan are needed (E07-F13, E07-F17; counsel).

An external definition of 'conformant' does not exist today; the Army AO memo (2025-09, RECALL/MEDIUM) and NIST SP 800-53 AU/AC families are the only public anchors for the RBAC/audit rubric, so the rubric must be labelled as the bench's own until a government body endorses one.
architecture.hardest_problem: Making a synthetic, netem-driven score MEAN something to the people who own acceptance. Technically the hardest sub-problem is faithful, reproducible multi-node reconciliation scoring: attributing every CoT object observed on every node to a ground-truth emission across partitions and reconnect storms (object IDs re-used, stale-time semantics, mission-sync versus streaming paths, emulator clock drift, TAK Server's own dedupe and stale handling) so that 'duplicate', 'conflict', 'late' and 'lost' are counted identically run to run and match what a soldier would see. netem models bandwidth/latency/loss on a point-to-point link but not MANET dynamics (routing churn, hidden nodes, half-duplex contention), so the bench must be honest that it measures application behaviour under specified link states, not radio behaviour - EMANE/CORE narrows but does not close this gap without controlled waveform models. The non-technical half of the hardest problem dominates: no government body has said what a passing score is, and until one does the report is an opinion. That is why every milestone below tests sponsor existence, not feature completeness.

must_be_proprietary: Nothing needs to be closed for the design to work; the score file's finding is that any proprietary layer is replicable in weeks by Anduril, TAK Product Center, Ditto or a lab. The only assets worth holding privately (as know-how, not code) are: the curated scenario library calibrated against whatever real-exercise anecdotes the T&E advisor can share; the scoring rubric weights and the RBAC/audit checklist mapping to AO expectations; and the anonymised cross-vendor results dataset. Even these should be published in part, because openness is the credibility mechanism for this narrower version.

architecture.integration_burden: LOW for the bench itself (all public code, one host, Docker), MEDIUM per SUT (each vendor plugin needs an adapter script for roles/tags and an agreed set of 'security-relevant actions'; CoT feeds need a mapping to the ground-truth ledger; Lattice clients need sandbox credentials), and HIGH-and-uncontrollable for anything the government would need to accept: a lab would have to map the bench's scenarios to its own emulation effects, the AO would have to endorse the RBAC/audit rubric, and PdM ASaP would have to admit a third-party report into its pipeline. Expect 1-2 engineer-days per SUT onboarding once the adapters exist, 2-4 weeks for a Lattice or Ditto adapter, and months of relationship work for any government acceptance.

performance_metrics.metric: Scenario reproducibility (coefficient of variation of headline scores across 3 identical runs)
performance_metrics.target: < 5% CV on time-to-arrival P95 and exact match on duplicate/conflict counts
performance_metrics.why: A score nobody can reproduce is an anecdote; reproducibility is the only differentiator against 'fixing the code live at Ivy Sting' (DVIDS 2026-03-30)

performance_metrics.metric: Link fidelity (configured vs measured throughput, latency and loss per link)
performance_metrics.target: within 10% of configured values from 1 Mbps to 1 kbps; partitions start within 1 s of schedule
performance_metrics.why: The DARPA FLUID 1 Mbps-1 kbps regime (2025-03-28) is the public DDIL definition buyers recognise; the bench must demonstrably hit it

performance_metrics.metric: Time-to-arrival of priority CoT objects after reconnect (P50/P95 per node)
performance_metrics.target: measured to +/-1 s across all nodes; report, do not prescribe, since no government threshold exists
performance_metrics.why: This is the number a commander feels ('lag under denied conditions', G29 current_workflow step 4) and the one a lab could compare across 50-80 vendors

performance_metrics.metric: Duplicate and conflicting objects after reconnect (per 1,000 ground-truth objects)
performance_metrics.target: zero false positives in the ledger; SUT results reported as raw counts
performance_metrics.why: Duplicate tracks after reconnect are a classic sync failure that TAK Server dedupe, mission sync and vendor feeds each handle differently

performance_metrics.metric: Object loss and ordering violations under a 30-minute partition at 4 kbps
performance_metrics.target: complete accounting of every ledger object (delivered / late / lost / superseded)
performance_metrics.why: Shows whether a feed degrades gracefully or silently drops data, which today is discovered only at events

performance_metrics.metric: Reconnect saturation (peak offered load / link capacity during the first 60 s after reconnect)
performance_metrics.target: reported as a ratio with time series; flag > 1.0 sustained > 10 s
performance_metrics.why: Reconnect storms are what break real tactical links; vendors rarely script them (G29 current_workflow step 2)

performance_metrics.target: 10 ATAK-CIV emulator nodes + 2 TAK Servers on a 64 GB host without emulator starvation
performance_metrics.why: A bench a vendor can run on one machine before a sprint is the entire value proposition

performance_metrics.target: < 15 minutes from YAML to a running scenario; full 30-minute scenario plus report in < 45 minutes
performance_metrics.why: Pre-sprint engineers will not adopt a bench that takes a day to configure

performance_metrics.target: 100% of the Mission API / Lattice endpoints the SUT actually calls are exercised; schema-level lint/breaking checks pass or list violations
performance_metrics.why: Undocumented or misused APIs were a top Jailbreak failure class (DefenseScoop 2026-05-29)

performance_metrics.target: every declared role x action pair tested; percent of security-relevant actions producing an audit record, mapped to a NIST SP 800-53 AU-2-style list
performance_metrics.why: Missing access control and logging were the AO's stated reason for the 'very high risk' NGC2 rating (CNBC 2025-10-03, RECALL/MEDIUM)

performance_metrics.target: OSCAL-style JSON validates against schema; cosign signature verifies; SBOM lists 100% of plugin dependencies detected by Syft
performance_metrics.why: ISSMs and pipeline owners need machine-checkable evidence, not PDFs

mvp.demo: A single-host, Dockerised 'TAK DDIL bench' demonstrated live and published on GitHub: 8-10 ATAK-CIV nodes (emulators plus 2-4 physical phones) and two TAK Servers behind netem profiles stepping from 1 Mbps to 4 kbps, a scripted 30-minute partition and reconnect storm, three public/open-source ATAK plugins and one synthetic UAS CoT feed run through the same scenario, producing side-by-side scored reports (time-to-arrival, duplicates/conflicts, loss, saturation); a contract-test CLI run against the same feed's Mission API usage and, if the Lattice licence permits, a Lattice sandbox client; and the plugin conformance module run against one open-source plugin to emit a signed OSCAL-style RBAC/audit/SBOM bundle. The demo is shown to (1) three or four MatrixSpace/Adyton-class vendors facing the next Jailbreak-series or PdM ASaP onboarding date, (2) a C5ISR Center or ATEC T&E contact via a NetModX / Reveille Forge / xTech application, and (3) a Team Anduril or Team Lockheed T&E engineer - and the demo's success criterion is a sponsor signal, not applause.
must_prove: That an independent, reproducible score (CV < 5% across repeated runs) exposes concrete failure classes - arrival delay, duplicate tracks after reconnect, silent loss, reconnect saturation, missing audit events - in real plugins and feeds BEFORE an event, matching the failure types reported from Jailbreak and Ivy Sting
That the bench runs end to end on one commodity machine in under 45 minutes per scenario, so a vendor engineer would actually use it in the week before a sprint

That the RBAC/audit bundle is machine-checkable (schema-valid OSCAL-style JSON, verified signature, complete SBOM) and that at least one ISSM/AO-adjacent reviewer says it is the shape of evidence they would accept

DECISIVE: that at least one named party with money or a vehicle - a vendor paying a fixed fee, PdM ASaP / PM C2 Applications, C5ISR Center, ATEC, Reveille Forge, TAK Product Center, or a prime T&E cell - commits in writing to use the report (paid readiness run, CRADA, evaluation agreement, task-order intent or pipeline inclusion) within 90 days of the first demo

build_plan.work: Set up TAK Server containers and 4 ATAK-CIV emulator nodes; implement the netem scenario runner with YAML link profiles (1 Mbps, 256 kbps, 64 kbps, 16 kbps, 4 kbps, 1 kbps) and partition scheduler; build the CoT traffic generator with ground-truth ledger (pytak/takproto); engage counsel (formation, EAR self-classification, technology control plan, copyleft review); start 90-day sponsor discovery: 15 outreach conversations targeted at Jailbreak-participant vendors, PdM ASaP / PM C2 Applications, C5ISR Center NetModX, ATEC industry-partner programme (NDM 2026-07-24), Reveille Forge, TAK Product Center.

Observer plugin on ATAK-CIV nodes; capture/ledger service and first sync scorer (time-to-arrival, loss, duplicates); scale to 8-10 nodes plus 2-4 physical phones; reproducibility runs (3x) and link-fidelity calibration; publish repo v0.1 with a 5-minute video; first three vendor demos; submit NetModX persistent-experimentation / Reveille Forge / xTech applications.

Contract-test CLI (Schemathesis against Mission API usage; buf lint/breaking against Lattice protos; Pact for CoT gateways); plugin conformance module v0.1 (Appium role drive, RBAC matrix, audit-event coverage, Syft SBOM, OSCAL-style bundle, cosign); run three open-source plugins and a synthetic UAS feed through the reference scenario; publish anonymised comparative results; demo to one prime T&E engineer and one government lab contact; ask each for a written statement of what evidence they would accept.

Harden: one-command install, 45-minute end-to-end run, docs; optional EMANE/CORE mode for a 3-hop topology; first paid fixed-fee readiness run if a vendor signs ($5-15k); decision gate against kill criteria; if a sponsor exists, scope Stage 2 (adapter for Lattice or Ditto, event slot); if not, freeze as a maintained open-source project and stop spending.

(Only if month-4 gate passes) Lattice or Ditto adapter, second scenario family (division-to-battalion multi-server federation), CRADA/evaluation-agreement paperwork with the sponsor, NIST SP 800-171 self-assessment planning if CUI is in prospect.

(Only if gate passed) Field-adjacent demonstration at the sponsor's venue or a NetModX / Reveille Forge slot with commercial radios in the loop; publish the sponsor-endorsed rubric; decide whether the residual business is a service line or a joinable team (acqui-hire / prime T&E subcontract).

kill_criteria: By day 45: fewer than 10 substantive conversations with target buyers (Jailbreak-participant vendors, PdM ASaP / PM C2 Applications, C5ISR Center, ATEC, Reveille Forge, TAK Product Center, prime T&E) or none of them names a budget, pipeline step or vehicle through which a third-party DDIL/conformance report could be consumed -> stop building beyond the open-source v0.1

By day 90 after first demo: no vendor has paid a fixed fee (>= $5,000) for a readiness run AND no government or prime party has signed a CRADA, evaluation agreement, task-order intent or pipeline-inclusion letter -> freeze the project as an open-source credibility asset; do not raise or spend further
By month 4: the bench cannot achieve < 5% CV reproducibility or < 10% link fidelity across 1 Mbps-1 kbps on one host -> the technical premise (a comparable score) fails; stop

At any point: a government body (C5ISR Center, TAK Product Center, PdM ASaP, Anduril for Lattice) publishes an equivalent open bench or declares its own report the only accepted evidence -> stop and contribute upstream instead

At any point: counsel finds the Lattice SDK licence prohibits third-party benchmarking/publication or the TAK Server/ATAK-CIV copyleft terms make the intended open-source release non-viable -> drop the affected module; if both, reassess whether any residual asset remains
Total spend cap: $60,000 excluding founder stipends before a signed sponsor exists; exceeding it without a sponsor is itself a kill

capital_map.does_250k_reach_next_fundable_milestone: YES, with a large margin - but the binding constraint is not money. Stages 0 and 1 together cost $38k-$84k (typically about $60k including stipends), which is the next milestone: a published, reproducible open-source TAK DDIL bench with a signed conformance bundle PLUS the result of the 90-day sponsor test. $250k would also cover the low end of Stage 2 ($120k-$300k) if a sponsor emerges. However, the score file's verdict is that no requirement owner, budget line or vehicle exists, so the 'fundable' event is not a technical deliverable but an external signal: a paying vendor, a CRADA/evaluation agreement with PdM ASaP, C5ISR Center, ATEC or Reveille Forge, or a prime T&E subcontract. The founders should cap spend at $60k (excluding stipends) until that signal exists, and treat the remaining ~$190k as reserved for a different opportunity. If the signal never comes, $250k does not change the outcome; it only funds a longer consultancy.
capital_map.next_milestone: Published v0.3 bench with reproducible comparative results for 3+ SUTs and one signed OSCAL-style conformance bundle, AND a documented answer to the decisive doubt within 90 days of first demo: either (a) >= 1 paid readiness run (>= $5k) plus >= 1 written government/prime commitment (CRADA, evaluation agreement, pipeline inclusion or task-order intent), which unlocks Stage 2; or (b) neither, which freezes the project as a credibility asset
capital_map.assumptions: All figures HYPOTHESIS unless noted. Hardware prices are RECALL (not re-verified this session). Founder stipends at student rates; U.S.-person T&E advisor at $150-250/hour fractional or equity. No PoR radio data, waveform models or CUI in Stages 0-1. Vendor readiness fees of $5-15k per run (INFERENCE from the score file's $5-25k range). Ditto SDK cost unknown (Public evidence insufficient). Lattice SDK licence terms unverified (EGRESS_BLOCKED); the Lattice module may have to be dropped. SBIR remains unavailable until the cap table meets 13 CFR 121.702 (E07-F3); OTA/CSO routes carry no ownership test but export-control and FOCI reviews apply - counsel, no legal determination. Government resources its own DDIL test (C5ISR Center Radio Rodeo 2026-03/04; Reveille Forge 2026-07; ATEC and APG/Huntsville SILs), so Stage 3+ is a hypothesis with no public evidence of a funder.

engineering_risks.risk: netem models point-to-point link states, not MANET radio dynamics (routing churn, contention, half-duplex), so scores may not predict field behaviour
engineering_risks.mitigation: State scope honestly ('application behaviour under specified link states'); add an EMANE/CORE mode with generic models for multi-hop topologies in month 4; calibrate scenarios with the T&E advisor; treat any sponsor-supplied emulation effects as the calibration target in Stage 2

engineering_risks.risk: Android emulators diverge from physical devices (timers, background limits, radio stack), corrupting time-to-arrival and reconnect behaviour
engineering_risks.mitigation: Mix 2-4 physical phones with emulators in every run; report emulator/physical split; measure emulator-vs-phone delta as a bench metric

engineering_risks.risk: Attribution errors in the ledger (CoT UID reuse, stale-time semantics, mission-sync versus streaming paths, TAK Server dedupe) produce false duplicates or losses
engineering_risks.mitigation: Tag every synthetic object with a bench-unique detail attribute plus emission time; validate the scorer against a zero-degradation control run that must score perfect; publish the counting rules

engineering_risks.risk: TAK Server / ATAK-CIV version drift and CIV-vs-GOV/MIL behaviour differences make results non-comparable over time
engineering_risks.mitigation: Pin versions per scenario and embed them in the report; keep a compatibility matrix; state explicitly that GOV/MIL builds are out of scope

engineering_risks.risk: Lattice SDK licence (updated 2026-07-31, terms unverified) may forbid publishing benchmark results or third-party test tooling
engineering_risks.mitigation: Counsel reads the licence before any Lattice work; keep the Lattice module optional and separable; fall back to TAK-only and Ditto adapters

engineering_risks.risk: Copyleft terms of TAK Server / ATAK-CIV may constrain how the bench is packaged and licensed
engineering_risks.mitigation: Keep bench code in separate processes communicating over sockets/APIs; license the bench itself permissively (Apache-2.0) where possible; counsel review before release

engineering_risks.risk: No authoritative definition of 'conformant' for RBAC/audit; the rubric is the founders' opinion and can be dismissed
engineering_risks.mitigation: Anchor every check to a public control (NIST SP 800-53 AU-2/AC-3-style), publish the mapping, and ask an ISSM/AO-adjacent reviewer to critique it in month 3; the demo's purpose is to get a government party to endorse or correct the rubric

engineering_risks.risk: Vendors 'teach to the test' or dispute scores, turning the bench into a liability
engineering_risks.mitigation: Randomise partition timings within declared bounds; publish counting rules; anonymise comparative results; frame outputs as diagnostics, not certification

engineering_risks.risk: Host resource starvation with 10 emulators plus servers skews timing
engineering_risks.mitigation: Cap at the measured node count where CPU steal is < 10%; use a 64 GB host; move to a cloud VM for larger runs; report host utilisation in every run

engineering_risks.risk: Clock alignment across nodes for sub-second time-to-arrival
engineering_risks.mitigation: All emulators share the host clock; physical phones sync via NTP to the host before each run; report residual offset

engineering_risks.risk: Deemed-export or CUI exposure if a lab shares link profiles, waveform models or traces with the non-U.S.-person founder
engineering_risks.mitigation: Technology control plan from month 1: controlled inputs handled only by the U.S.-person advisor/engineer in a segregated enclave; the bench stays synthetic-only until counsel clears anything else

engineering_risks.risk: A government body or platform owner publishes its own bench and the founders' work is stranded
engineering_risks.mitigation: This is an explicit kill criterion; the mitigation is speed to publication (month 2) and contributing upstream so the founders' names travel with the work

engineering_risks.risk: The whole effort produces credibility but no sponsor, and drifts into unpaid support
engineering_risks.mitigation: Hard $60k cap and the 90-day sponsor test; pre-agreed stop decision; treat the asset as a portfolio piece for joining a prime T&E cell, TAK plugin shop or NGC2 sub-vendor
